open_points.subject: A18 symbolic-link handling for SQLite-managed files
open_points.text: “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link” contradicts “A link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written” and `symlink_inside(data_directory) -> refused`.
open_points.question: What must happen when a symbolic link is placed at a SQLite-managed database or journal path after the start-time walk?
options: The store must detect it and fail the call with nothing written
SQLite-managed paths are exceptions to the later-link rule and formal invariant
The kernel must use a SQLite access mechanism that provides no-follow guarantees
open_points.default_guess: Require the store to detect the link and fail the call without writing.

open_points.subject: SQLite-managed file boundary
open_points.text: “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite”
open_points.question: Which SQLite-created files are covered by this exception: only the main database and rollback journal, or also WAL, shared-memory, temporary and other auxiliary files, and which journal mode is fixed?
options: Fix rollback-journal mode and exempt only the database and rollback journal
Include every SQLite-managed auxiliary file in the exception
Name an explicit closed list of permitted SQLite files and modes
open_points.default_guess: Fix one journal mode and name a closed list of SQLite-managed files.

open_points.subject: A20 non-Linux start behavior
open_points.text: “The kernel does not test the host: on any other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start stops” conflicts with the earlier start steps using Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`, where “no code asks whether the flag exists and there is no mode without it”.
open_points.question: On a non-Linux host, is behavior outside the contract, or must the process reliably reach the sandbox probe and stop there rather than failing earlier while loading the installation or store?
options: Non-Linux behavior is outside the contract
Earlier steps must remain executable and the sandbox probe must be the stated refusal
An explicit host check must precede all Linux-specific operations
open_points.default_guess: Treat non-Linux behavior as outside the runtime contract and remove the guaranteed sandbox-probe failure claim.

open_points.subject: Linux-only release constraint
open_points.text: “A release runs on Linux and on no other host (owner, 2026-10-18). The kernel does not test the host”
open_points.question: What owner or capability enforces that the release cannot be installed or launched on a non-Linux host?
options: The release build or packaging process enforces the target OS
The installer enforces the target OS
Nothing enforces it; Linux is only a documented deployment precondition
open_points.default_guess: Assign enforcement to the release build and packaging process.
